Subject: Something afoot in the City

SOMETHING AFOOT IN THE CITY
There's something going on in the City. It's hard to divine precisely what it is, but it seems to centre on the banks' need for more liquidity.

We know the Bank of England, despite its �23bn largesse with Northern Rock (so far), is reluctant to keep pumping more cash into the system. We also know that there was a meeting of senior bankers at the Bank of England yesterday. All my usual sources have gone to ground today, which is another surefire suggestion that something is afoot.

The tangible facts relate to Barclays' loss, at one point, of 8 per cent on the stock market, and reports that the Citigroup has got capital problems. Faisal Islam is out in the City, ferreting about, and we'll see what we can hone in on at seven.

Barclays shares plummet: http://tinyurl.com/2tqwtj

ANOTHER BLAIR CONTROVERSY
We have an interesting new development in the fortunes of Sir Ian Blair, Metropolitan Police commissioner, whose force was yesterday found guilty of endangering the public over the death of Jean Charles de menezes. Another unfortunate controversy on his watch. I can't say more at this stage, but well worth tuning in.

TALKING WITH THE PKK
Abroad, Condi Rice has been in Turkey, reassuring the Turks that America understands their concerns about the radical PKK rebels in northern Iraq. We have an exclusive interview with the leader of the PKK tonight. Again, to protect its exclusivity I must hold back on this one.

PAPWORTH HEART OPS ON HOLD
Serious floods in Mexico have engulfed a region the size of Wales (as they say) and displaced hundreds of thousands of people. Back home, we're looking at the decision to close the heart transplant ward at Papworth hospital - one of the great leaders in this sort of surgery. They're concerned that their death rate within 30 days following major heart transplant surgery, normally one in 10, has fallen to seven in 20.

Mexico floods trap thousands: http://tinyurl.com/2tnbhn

A NEW CHAPTER FOR RICHARD AND JUDY
And finally, my good friends Richard and Judy are vacating the space that I used to intrude upon from time to time in the late afternoons. But they're not leaving Channel 4 altogether. It seems their book projects will continue in another form elsewhere in the schedule.

25 YEARS OLD
We shall continue in the same form on this, our 25th anniversary night, at seven. And I calculate that it is probably somewhere around my 4,500th programme. But hey, who's counting? (me! - Ed.)

Jon's most memorable Channel 4 News moments: http://tinyurl.com/2o5whp

Channel 4 News at 25: changing faces http://tinyurl.com/3yu3oc

AND ON MORE4 NEWS WITH KYLIE MORRIS
We talk to a former police chief who DID resign when his officers shot the wrong man, despite the fact that an inquiry found HE wasn�t to blame. Does he think Sir Ian Blair should go?�

And the latest twist to reality TV? MOSQUE idol. May the best minaret win.

Join us at 8pm.
